column1: # ── Curated additions — added by hand 2026-08-05, keep on regeneration ──────────
# The generated world-city layer above admits only cities with population ≥ 100 000.
# That threshold is correct globally but blind in Denmark's own neighbourhood: an
# Øresund or Schleswig-Holstein site then resolves no further than its country row,
# whose centroid is the capital — "Lund, Sweden" was reported as 522 km away (the
# Stockholm centroid) instead of 39 km, and sub-100k German sites such as Bad Homburg
# resolved to nothing at all and were never filtered.
# The rows below are therefore deliberately BELOW the generator's threshold. They are
# NOT reproducible by re-running the ≥ 100 000 filter — a future regeneration must
# either carry this block over verbatim or lower the threshold for DE/SE/NO/CZ.
# Every coordinate and population was fetched from GeoNames (www.geonames.org public
# city pages / getJSON) and cross-checked against OpenStreetMap Nominatim and, where
# available, Wikipedia; no row deviates from its cross-check by more than 0.03°.
# Populations are GeoNames city-proper figures, matching the generated rows above.
# Schleswig has no GeoNames city page; its figures come from Nominatim + Wikipedia.
# GeoNames data remains CC-BY 4.0 (see the file header).
# Four existing rows also gained a short-form alias in this pass (Almere Stad→Almere,
# Frankfurt am Main→Frankfurt, Ludwigshafen am Rhein→Ludwigshafen, Klagenfurt am
# Wörthersee→Klagenfurt): GeoNames stores the long official toponym, so the everyday
# name listings actually use resolved to the country centroid. Those alias edits sit on
